facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility is a generative AI-first application for Generative Engine Optimization (also called Answer Engine Optimization), designed to help brands enhance their visibility, accuracy, and influence in AI-driven search environments.
facts.supports: Adobe defines Brand Visibility as its application for Generative Engine Optimization, built to improve a brand's visibility, accuracy and influence in AI-driven search.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: It provides insights into brand presence in AI-generated answers, offers prescriptive content recommendations, and automates optimization fixes.
facts.supports: The product reports on brand presence in AI-generated answers, recommends content changes and automates fixes.

facts.title: Experience League: Prompt Management
facts.quote: Prompt Management helps you define, organize, and maintain the prompts used to measure your brand’s visibility across AI platforms.
facts.supports: Customers define, organize and maintain the prompts used to measure visibility.

facts.title: Experience League: Prompt Management
facts.quote: Powered by recommendations from Semrush, Google Search Console, Synthetic Personas, and Citation Attempt, Prompt Strategy surfaces topics where your brand has an opportunity to improve visibility as well as topics where your brand already performs well.
facts.supports: Suggested prompts and topics come from four sources: Semrush, Google Search Console, Synthetic Personas and Citation Attempt.

facts.title: Experience League: Best Practices for Categories, Topics, Prompts, and Others
facts.quote: Prompts can be added to Adobe Brand Visibility manually or via bulk upload using the provided .csv template.
facts.supports: Prompts can be added by hand or by bulk CSV upload.

facts.title: Experience League: Quick Start
facts.quote: Customers who activate the trial on or after April 1, 2026 can use up to 100 prompts, one domain, and can deploy optimizations across up to 50 URLs for a single opportunity type.
facts.supports: The free trial is limited to 100 prompts and one domain; Adobe's pages give no prompt limit for paid licenses.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Presence (Trial)
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility currently supports ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Co-pilot, Google Gemini, and Perplexity.
facts.supports: The Brand Presence (Trial) page names six AI engines for the Platform filter: ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini and Perplexity.

facts.title: Experience League: AI Visibility
facts.quote: AI Visibility currently supports analysis across ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, and Gemini.
facts.supports: The Semrush-powered AI Visibility section covers four engines (ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode, Gemini); Perplexity and Copilot are not named there.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: Brand Visibility measures the percentage of prompts where your brand is mentioned.
facts.supports: The Brand Visibility metric (formerly Visibility Score) is the percentage of tracked prompts where the brand is mentioned.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: Calculated using the same methodology as the trial experience - each response is counted once if your brand is mentioned.
facts.supports: Mentions counts each AI response once if the brand is mentioned.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: Calculated using the same methodology as the trial experience - each response is counted once if your website is cited.
facts.supports: Citations counts each AI response once if the customer's website is cited.

facts.title: Experience League: What's New in Adobe Brand Visibility
facts.quote: Adobe Brand Visibility now tracks the metric Source Visibility, which reflects how often your website is used as a source in AI answers.
facts.supports: Source Visibility reports how often the customer's website is used as a source in AI answers.

facts.title: Experience League: What's New in Adobe Brand Visibility
facts.quote: Share of Voice now reflects your visibility weighted by search demand and ranking position - a more traffic-oriented measure than a simple mention share.
facts.supports: Share of Voice is visibility weighted by search demand and ranking position, not a simple share of mentions.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Presence (powered by Semrush)
facts.quote: Sentiment is evaluated at the aspect level, allowing a single AI-generated response to contain both positive and negative sentiment for different aspects of your brand.
facts.supports: Sentiment is scored per aspect of the brand within each AI response.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Presence (Trial)
facts.quote: The relative prominence of your brand in AI responses, calculated as an average across all weeks.
facts.supports: Position (Trial dashboard) is the brand's relative prominence in AI responses, averaged across weeks.

facts.title: Experience League: Brands Management
facts.quote: Tracking other brands enables Brand Presence to compare your performance against other brands within the same market.
facts.supports: Competitors are set up as tracked 'other brands' (brand name and website) in Brands Management and compared within the same market.

facts.title: Experience League: Best Practices for Categories, Topics, Prompts, and Others
facts.quote: With other brands to track, you can see how often other brands are mentioned alongside your brand in different regions and categories and compare their visibility to your own.
facts.supports: Tracked brands are compared on how often they are mentioned alongside the customer's brand, by region and category.

facts.title: Experience League: AI Visibility
facts.quote: It puts your brand side by side with the other brands you choose, then shows exactly where those brands earn mentions and citations that your brand doesn’t.
facts.supports: Market Comparison (AI Visibility) shows where chosen competitor brands earn mentions and citations the customer's brand does not.

facts.title: Experience League: URL Inspector
facts.quote: It combines visibility, agentic traffic, and referral data at the URL level to give you a granular view of which URLs are cited and how often they appear in responses.
facts.supports: URL Inspector shows which of the customer's URLs are cited in AI answers and how often.

facts.title: Experience League: URL Inspector
facts.quote: The trending URLs competing for citations view, highlights external URLs that are currently cited in answers relevant to your brand, measuring who is winning citations in your space.
facts.supports: URL Inspector also lists external (third-party) URLs cited in answers relevant to the brand.

facts.title: Experience League: AI Visibility
facts.quote: opens the full AI answer behind a prompt: the response text, whether your brand was mentioned, which brands were mentioned, whether your site was cited and the source URLs behind the answer.
facts.supports: For a prompt, the Details view shows the full AI answer, brands mentioned, whether the site was cited and the source URLs.

facts.title: Experience League: Agentic Traffic
facts.quote: The Agentic Traffic dashboard shows how AI agents (crawlers and chatbots) interact with your site.
facts.supports: Agentic Traffic shows how AI crawlers and chatbots interact with the customer's site.

facts.title: Experience League: Agentic Traffic
facts.quote: The data used by this dashboard is sourced from the CDN logs so you must configure CDN log forwarding in order to display metrics.
facts.supports: Agentic Traffic data comes from CDN logs, so CDN log forwarding must be configured.

facts.title: Experience League: Agentic Traffic
facts.quote: No Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is processed or stored at any stage of CDN log ingestion or subsequent data handling.
facts.supports: Adobe states no PII is processed or stored from the CDN logs.

facts.title: Experience League: Referral Traffic
facts.quote: Referral Traffic shows how visitors arrive at your site from external platforms, AI citations, and referral links.
facts.supports: Referral Traffic shows visitors arriving from external platforms, AI citations and referral links.

facts.title: Experience League: Referral Traffic
facts.quote: The total traffic from human users who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.
facts.supports: The 'Referral Traffic from LLM's' metric is human users who clicked citation links in AI-generated answers.

facts.title: Experience League: Referral Traffic
facts.quote: If your organization is on a paid offer, you can connect Adobe Analytics or Google Analytics 4 (GA4) to add data that measures AI-driven discovery and site engagement.
facts.supports: Referral Traffic is built from CDN logs by default; paid customers can add Adobe Analytics or GA4 data for the Business Impact tab.

facts.title: Experience League: Optimization opportunities
facts.quote: Optimization opportunities are automatically detected insights that show where your site and external presence can be improved to increase brand visibility in AI search.
facts.supports: Opportunities are automatically detected insights on where the site and off-site presence can be improved.

facts.title: Experience League: Optimization opportunities
facts.quote: These optimizations include on-page fixes (adding structured content, canonicals, or summaries), technical adjustments (unblocking AI crawlers or resolving errors) and influencing content on third-party authoritative sites.
facts.supports: Opportunities cover on-page content fixes, technical adjustments and off-site (third-party) content.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: Each prompt is executed on a recurring basis across supported AI platforms, allowing Adobe Brand Visibility to monitor how your brand appears in AI-generated responses and how that performance changes over time.
facts.supports: Data is collected by executing each Prompt Library prompt on a recurring basis across the supported AI platforms.

facts.title: Experience League: Brand Visibility Overview
facts.quote: It provides ongoing visibility measurements for the prompts you actively monitor, enabling you to evaluate performance, identify trends, and understand how AI systems represent your brand over time.
facts.supports: Brand Visibility reports on the prompts the customer actively monitors, not on every user conversation.

facts.title: Experience League: Quick Start
facts.quote: The exact prompts you ask LLMs are not publicly available because they are not disclosed by the LLMs.
facts.supports: Adobe notes that the exact prompts people ask LLMs are not disclosed by the LLMs; this is the closest statement on Adobe's pages that reporting is not based on real user conversations.

facts.title: Experience League: Prompt Management
facts.quote: Newly added prompts must be processed before they begin contributing to Brand Presence metrics. Depending on the size of your prompt library, this can take up to 24 hours.
facts.supports: Newly added prompts can take up to 24 hours to start contributing to Brand Presence metrics.

facts.title: Experience League: Customer Configuration
facts.quote: Brand Presence data for newly added prompts will appear during the next scheduled data refresh, which typically runs at the beginning of each week.
facts.supports: On the legacy Customer Configuration page, Adobe says the scheduled Brand Presence data refresh typically runs at the beginning of each week.

facts.title: Experience League: Brands Management
facts.quote: You can configure multiple markets for each brand to monitor how your brand appears across different regions and languages.
facts.supports: Each brand can be tracked in multiple markets, each a country or region plus a language and website.

not_found: claim 3: a list of AI platforms for the paid, Semrush-powered Brand Presence dashboard. Its page (dashboards/brand-visibility/brand-presence-semrush) says only 'supported AI platforms' and 'broader AI platform coverage'; the six-engine list including Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot is on the Brand Presence (Trial) page, and the AI Visibility and Semrush Suggestions pages name four engines without Perplexity or Copilot. No Brand Visibility page names Claude, Meta AI or Grok as a tracked answer engine (Claude appears only as a crawler / referral source).

claim 9: how often tracked prompts are run. The current pages (brand-visibility-overview, prompt-management) say only 'on a recurring basis'; no daily or weekly figure. The only cadence is on the legacy Customer Configuration page (weekly refresh, 'typically runs at the beginning of each week'). Also not stated: how many times each prompt is run per cycle, or whether answers are collected through the consumer apps or APIs.

claim 9: a list of supported countries, regions or languages. Brands Management says a market is a country or region plus a language plus a website, and Brand Presence (powered by Semrush) mentions market-language combinations such as US-en, but no page lists which markets or languages are available.

claim 2: a prompt limit for paid licenses. Only the free-trial limit (100 prompts, or 200 for trials activated before April 1, 2026) is on the Quick Start page; the Impact Measurement Engine page mentions a 'Prompt quota' without a number.

claim 4: a formula for the metrics. Adobe gives one-line definitions only; the trial page says the visibility score weights mentions, citations, sentiment and rank without giving the weights, and the enhanced Position metric is not defined on the Semrush-powered Brand Presence page (Position is defined only on the Trial page and in Best Practices).

claim 9: an explicit sentence that the product does not capture real end-user conversations. Closest are the Quick Start note that prompts asked of LLMs are not disclosed by the LLMs, and the statements that Brand Presence measures the prompts in the customer's Prompt Library. Note that the Semrush Suggestions page does describe 'the real user prompts Semrush observed', which is Semrush's prompt database, not the customer's own users.
FAQ: there is no standalone Brand Visibility FAQ page; FAQs sit inside What's New, Impact Measurement Engine, the integration pages and individual opportunity pages.
cautions: Two editions with different dashboards and metrics: Trial versus the enhanced (paid) experience powered by Semrush. 'The Brand Presence experience varies based on your Adobe Brand Visibility edition.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/brand-visibility/brand-visibility-overview

Platform lists differ by page: the six engines including Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot are named on the Trial page (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/brand-visibility/brand-presence-trial); AI Visibility names only ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews, Google AI Mode and Gemini (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/ai-visibility). Do not claim Perplexity or Copilot for the Semrush-powered views from these pages.

Visibility Score was renamed and redefined: in the enhanced experience 'Brand Visibility' is 'measured purely as how often your brand is mentioned. Previously, the score also factored citations, position, and sentiment.' Share of Voice also has a new methodology, so values differ from the trial. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/essentials/whats-new

The weekly-refresh quote (bv.collection.5) is from a page marked 'This page is retained for legacy reference only. Configuration has moved to the Brands Management dashboard.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/customer-configuration

Regions: 'Not all regions will be available at launch.' appears on the Brand Presence (Trial) and URL Inspector pages. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/url-inspector

Prompt suggestions language (legacy page FAQ): 'The pipeline currently generates prompts in English only. Multi-language support will be added in a future release.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/customer-configuration

Agentic Traffic and Referral Traffic are blank without CDN log forwarding: 'Without CDN log forwarding, the Agentic Traffic dashboard is blank.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/agentic-traffic ; the Referral Traffic Business Impact tab needs Adobe Analytics, GA4 or CJA and a paid offer. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/referral-traffic

Opportunities: 'Edge based auto-optimization is currently available in Early Access for select opportunities.' and 'Enrich Product Catalog (Beta)' on https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/opportunities/opportunities-overview ; Add Multimedia Transcript Summaries is also Early Access. Optimize at Edge delivers to ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude agents only (https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/resources/optimize-at-edge/overview).

Trial terms: 'Access is provided on an "as-is" and "as-available" basis, and may be modified, limited or removed at any time.' Trial is 100 prompts, one domain, 50 URLs for one opportunity type. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/essentials/quick-start

Custom tags are paid-only: 'Custom tags are available only to paying Adobe Brand Visibility customers.' Multiple brands and additional domains are enhanced-edition features. https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/dashboards/brands-management
Category changes reset history: 'changes to categories reset historical data.' https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/brand-visibility/using/essentials/best-practices-topics-prompts

Some pages still say 'LLM Optimizer' in body text (for example Prompt Management: 'the prompt library that LLM Optimizer runs on a recurring basis'); avoid quoting those lines if the old name would confuse a client.
